title: Codex-first model routing: fix broken enforcement layer
description: Codex delegation ran at ~3% of delegable work. Root causes: (1) $CODEX_PLUGIN never exported, so the documented readiness check errored and sessions invoked the fallback clause and worked inline; (2) the two routing hooks still encoded the pre-Codex table and ExitPlanMode actively instructed inline Opus builds; (3) hooks lived untracked outside cc-harness with no selftest; (4) no gate fired at the inline-edit moment.
design: Track hooks/ and scripts/ in cc-harness and link them via install.sh. Resolve the plugin root with a semver-aware resolver instead of an unset env var. Add a once-per-session first-edit gate. Every guard gets a falsifiable selftest.
acceptance_criteria: All selftests green at real exit codes; each proven red by mutation; a fresh headless session delegates to Codex instead of working inline.

title: Every selftest exits 0 when it aborts mid-run — the whole gate can't go red
description: Measured 2026-09-03 across all ten gates (scripts/*selftest*.sh + hooks/selftest.sh): each installs , and cleanup's final command (rm -rf on a temp dir) succeeds, replacing the status of a script dying from set -e/set -u. Injecting an unbound-variable reference immediately after the trap line makes every one of them print the error and exit 0. So a typo, an unset variable, a missing binary, or any abort partway through a suite reads as PASS. This is the exact disease rules/verification-integrity.md exists to prevent, sitting in the apparatus that enforces it — and CLAUDE.md's claim that 'local green means every selftest passes at a real exit code' is not true for the abort class. Note the assertion path is unaffected: a failing assertion still exits 1 correctly. Only aborts are swallowed.
acceptance_criteria: Each selftest's EXIT trap preserves the dying status (capture $? first, exit with it last). Proven by injecting an abort after the trap line in a copy of each and observing a non-zero exit — the same measurement that found this, re-run green.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #39 (d2978cc). All ten gates now fail on abort; verified in three directions (clean=0, real failure=1, injected abort=non-zero).

title: [bug] codex-brokers.sh: unregistered broker defaults to STALE, so a missing state store makes --reap-stale kill LIVE brokers
description: Found by adversarial review of stemlab PR #404, confirmed on the machine: with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA unset (it is not in any shell profile or settings.json — the harness injects it per-plugin), every broker including ones serving a running job reads verdict=STALE, and --reap-stale SIGKILLs the broker and its codex app-server child. Absence of a registration must never imply safe-to-kill. Fix: verdict UNKNOWN (never reaped) for a broker whose registration was not found but whose cwd exists; STALE only when independently verifiable (cwd missing, or cwd under TMPDIR); and refuse to reap at all when zero broker.json files were discovered.

title: codex-jobs.sh --active lists dead-pid jobs as active
description: scripts/codex-jobs.sh --active reports jobs whose worker pid is dead as if they were running. Observed 2026-09-04 from a stemlab session: task-mtk4f451-vqhgcs and task-mtk3iovo-d1vnaj (workspace /private/tmp/cc-harness-credential-free-pr-gates, 2026-09-02), task-mtj3igy3-73iooj (rudderstack ds-audit-harness, 2026-09-01), review-mtik1ban-qmd342 (stemlab-worktrees/vgek-review, 2026-09-01) — all four printed with status 'running' and a pid annotated (dead) in the same row. Per ~/.claude/rules/codex-job-status-integrity.md a record whose tracked pid is gone while status is running/queued is an orphan, not a pending result. Listing it under --active is the instrument failure that rule's 'instruments must distinguish healthy from not looking' section describes: --active is consulted precisely when nobody is watching, and it currently cannot tell 'still executing' from 'the worker died days ago'. Note the row already computes and prints pid liveness, so the data is present and only the filter ignores it.
acceptance_criteria: --active excludes records whose tracked pid is not alive; such a record is surfaced as orphaned/unknown rather than active (or omitted with a count), so an empty --active list means no live work rather than none detected; a negative control proves the filter bites — mutate a job record's pid to a dead one and watch it leave --active.
notes: Reported by the stemlab sl-0g0q session. Companion finding from the same day, filed separately by another session against stemlab: scripts/merge-gate.sh leaves a stale .build/merge-gate/last-summary.txt asserting a PASS for an earlier tree while a run is in flight. Same disease, opposite severity — that one actively asserts a green rather than failing to detect a red.

title: Codex build mailbox: let a sandboxed Codex turn get a real build/test result
description: Codex cannot run swift build or scripts/test.sh inside its sandbox (nested Seatbelt kills swift-plugin-server, so every @State/@Observable macro site fails to expand). Every stemlab handoff therefore returns UNVERIFIED code, and the orchestrator pays Claude tokens for a build -> collect errors -> --resume loop, repeatedly, for mistakes Codex would have caught itself if it could compile. A mailbox lets a sandboxed turn request a command run OUTSIDE the sandbox and read the result back, collapsing N Claude round trips into one. SECURITY: this is deliberately a hole in the sandbox, so the runner must execute only an allowlisted set of commands in a fixed workspace, never arbitrary text from the request.
design: Three parts: (1) a detached host-side runner that polls a mailbox dir; (2) a request/response file protocol; (3) a client the Codex prompt calls. Follows the codex-wait.sh precedent for detached polling. Load-bearing assumption to probe FIRST: can a sandboxed Codex turn write a request and block for a reply within one turn, while Claude is itself blocked on that task?
acceptance_criteria: A Codex task that cannot compile can obtain a real compiler error list from outside its sandbox within one turn; the runner refuses any command not on the allowlist, proven by a negative control; no path lets request content reach a shell as code.
notes: BLOCKED after adversarial review + direct verification. Two sandbox escapes reproduced on-machine (arbitrary host-file overwrite via a caller-planted log symlink; killing any same-user process via a forged runner.pid). Attempted fix committed as b66aca7 on claude/codex-build-mailbox (PR #38, now human/hold) but NOT ready: (1) start/status/stop all crash under bash 3.2 — 'local a=$1 b=$a/x' expands before assigning; (2) the forged-PID assertion is vacuously green because stop crashes before reaching the guard, and the suite never invokes start/status at all; (3) the fix assumes $TMPDIR is host-private, which is likely false for a workspace-write sandbox — UNVERIFIED and must be settled first; (4) unaddressed: mv of a consumed request to req-<id>.json.done follows a caller-planted symlink to a directory = write-anywhere primitive with caller-chosen content. Root cause is structural: the host trusts a directory the untrusted party writes. Next attempt: state under $HOME (not sandbox-writable), no PID file (runner holds an flock), refuse any delivery destination that exists as a symlink or directory. FIRST decide whether the feature is worth it at all — the orchestrator polling for a request file and running swift build itself buys the same token saving with zero host-side trust.

title: codex-jobs/brokers: silent exit on unresolvable plugin root, /private TMPDIR alias defeats STALE, single plugin-data root scanned
description: Fable 5.1 review of #31/#32. (1) codex-jobs.sh exits 0 with no output when the plugin root or state dir cannot be resolved - indistinguishable from 'no jobs' (verification-integrity: instruments must distinguish healthy from not looking). (2) isUnderTmp compares path.resolve() strings; macOS TMPDIR is /var/... while ps reports /private/var/..., so a broker under the real tmp dir is never STALE and --reap-stale skips exactly the plugin-test residue it exists for. (3) both scripts scan only $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA; a second plugin install (codex-openai-codex vs codex-inline) keeps its own data root, so --restart-idle could kill a broker whose active job is recorded elsewhere. Fix: stderr message + exit 1 for (1); realpath both sides for (2); scan sibling data roots for (3); selftest cases for each.

title: codex-dispatch-protocol: state that background workers/brokers are already setsid-detached; foreground is the only path a harness kill reaches
description: Measured 2026-09-02: harness timeout kills the Bash call's process group (plain child dead), a Node detached:true child (own session, ppid 1) survives. The plugin's spawnDetachedTaskWorker and spawnBrokerProcess both use detached:true, so no extra setsid wrapper is needed for --background; wrapping a FOREGROUND task in setsid would detach a worker no record tracks. Add this to the rule so nobody adds redundant or harmful setsid trickery.

title: Investigate transient Codex brokers spawned with a garbage --cwd (text from a Bash tool call)
description: Seen twice on 2026-09-01 while running codex-brokers-selftest from a stemlab session: an app-server-broker.mjs serve process appeared with --cwd '%s' and later with --cwd set to a chunk of the Bash tool call's own text; each self-terminated within a minute. No cc-harness hook invokes codex-companion (checked bd-ready-model-routing.sh, first-edit-codex-gate.sh, exitplan-model-routing.sh); plugin hooks are SessionStart/End/Stop only. Reproduce with codex-brokers.sh in a loop while a Bash call containing the literal '--cwd %s' runs; check the plugin's stop-review-gate-hook and any peer session's hooks. Harmless (STALE verdict, self-exits) but is exactly the ghost-state the dispatch protocol exists to prevent.
